items.stem: Distinguish between direct costs and indirect costs in a manufacturing business.
items.answer: Direct costs can be traced to each unit produced (materials, production wages, royalties); indirect costs are factory costs that cannot be traced to units (supervisors, factory rent, power).
items.markingKey: Direct – traceable to units [1]; indirect – cannot be traced [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the manufacturing account is prepared separately from the income statement.
items.answer: It shows the cost of producing the goods in the factory, separating production costs from selling and administration costs, so management can control factory costs.
items.markingKey: Shows cost of production [1]; control of factory costs [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain where each of the three types of inventory is used in the financial statements of a manufacturer.
items.answer: Raw materials: manufacturing account (materials consumed); work in progress: manufacturing account (adjusting total factory cost); finished goods: income statement (cost of sales); all three closing inventories are current assets.
items.markingKey: RM and WIP – manufacturing account [1]; FG – income statement [1]; all CA [1] [3]

items.stem: Explain why work in progress is valued at factory cost.
items.answer: Partly finished goods have absorbed materials, labour and overheads; valuing them at factory cost matches costs to the goods completed in each period.

Complete the statement: Goods are transferred from the factory at cost plus 25%. Closing finished goods at transfer price are $20,000. The unrealised profit is …
Explain why a provision for unrealised profit is needed when goods are transferred at a profit.
items.answer: The factory profit on goods still unsold has not been realised by a sale to an outside customer; the provision removes it so inventory is at cost and profit is not overstated.
items.markingKey: Profit not realised by external sale [1]; inventory at cost/profit not overstated [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why only the change in the provision for unrealised profit is charged in the income statement.
items.answer: The opening provision was charged in an earlier year; only the increase (or decrease) relates to the current year.
